details:
Pulse automates NASA ARSET's NISAR flood-mapping workflow, turning hours of specialist work into minutes. Users enter a research question, location, and two dates, and Pulse finds matching satellite images through NASA CMR and ASF, processes the study area, and compares radar data to identify possible flooding.

By analysing radar patterns, Pulse detects open water and flooded vegetation while marking areas hidden beneath dense forest as uncertain rather than incorrectly labelling them dry. Users can explore results, adjust flood thresholds, watch maps update live, and inspect individual pixels. Every decision and measurement is recorded to make studies transparent and repeatable, while GDACS flood alerts, NASA POWER rainfall, and OPERA surface-water data provide additional context.

Powered by ElevenLabs, Professor Pulse lets users navigate the platform and explore studies by voice, while a Claude-powered research assistant helps plan studies and test hypotheses against real measurements. AI guides the process but never invents scientific results.

Pulse also generates research papers with figures and downloadable mapping data. Our Peru demonstration was compared with NASA ARSET training examples, and the platform is built with Python, FastAPI, React, and Leaflet, supported by 333 automated Python tests and 53 browser checks.

Our goal is to make NASA satellite data accessible beyond specialist teams, with future applications in wetlands, agriculture, and land-subsidence monitoring.
